name: CropX Technologies
what_it_is: Israel-based soil-sensing and digital-agronomy company whose in-ground probes measure moisture, temperature, salinity (and, via acquired tech, nitrate) and feed an AI agronomy/irrigation platform. In March 2025 it launched 'Apex', a multi-depth sensor reading the full root-zone profile at 4-inch intervals.
backers: Founders incl. Tomer Tzach (CEO); investors incl. Finistere Ventures, Innovation Endeavors (Eric Schmidt), GreenSoil Investments, OurCrowd, Aliaxis, ICL Group, Flashpoint VC.
funding: ~$90.8M total raised across ~10 rounds from ~45-47 investors. Latest disclosed equity rounds predate 2025; recent activity is M&A (acquired Acclym/Agritask Sept 2025; EnGeniousAg nitrogen sensor 2024). Latest fresh-round size/date: n/a.
traction: Deployed in 50-70+ countries; ~1,200+ paying customers and ~8,500 installations since 2017. Reported ~40% water savings and ~10% yield uplift. Seven acquisitions consolidating a full-stack soil-to-agronomy platform.
reviews: Positive: praised for data-transmission reliability, sensor accuracy and easy DIY probe install; seen as a fast-growing consolidator. Negative: customers cite weak agronomy support after the sale; platform is broad/enterprise-leaning rather than low-cost; aggressive roll-up raises integration questions.
pricing: Hardware sensor + paid SaaS subscription (per-sensor/per-field annual fee); enterprise tiers. List pricing not public (n/a).
endo_take: Best-in-class incumbent and a partner/benchmark rather than a buy target; their multi-depth Apex is what a low-cost Indian sensor stack is measured against. Opportunity to partner on agronomy, threat if they push downmarket into India.
justification: Mature, global, full-stack soil-sensing leader still actively advancing.

name: Stenon (FarmLab)
what_it_is: German maker of FarmLab, a handheld spade-style device delivering real-time, in-situ soil analysis (mineral nitrogen, organic matter/SOC, moisture, temperature, texture) in seconds via optical spectroscopy + impedance sensing and AI, eliminating lab sampling.
backers: Founders incl. Dominic Roth & Niels Grabbert; investors incl. Founders Fund, The Production Board, Cherry Ventures, Atlantic Labs, Oyster Bay.
funding: ~$21.2M total: $20M Series A (Dec 2021, Founders Fund / The Production Board) + ~$1.05M seed. No new round disclosed 2024-2026 (latest round: n/a since 2021).
traction: Commercial deployments across Europe and Brazil (potato and row-crop growers); assembled in Germany with TUV and DLG certifications. Rental/usage model lowers adoption friction. Revenue figures not disclosed (n/a).
reviews: Positive: DLG-certified for mobile soil-tester accuracy; strong on physical parameters and a novel instant-NPK pitch. Negative: peer-reviewed 2024-25 field studies found poor temporal consistency and low correlation for mineral nitrogen, SOC and especially phosphorus — 'not yet suitable for precision nutrient management' per one study.
pricing: Device-as-a-service / rental rather than outright sale; per-use or subscription. Exact pricing not public (n/a).
endo_take: Closest technical analogue to Endo's in-field sensing thesis and a useful capability benchmark — validates the market but flags the hard accuracy ceiling on optical NPK/SOC. Mostly a learning reference and possible partner.
justification: Novel real-time soil spade, but stalled funding and contested accuracy.

name: Varaha
what_it_is: Gurugram, India-based carbon-removal developer and MRV platform combining remote sensing, ML and field science to quantify and verify regenerative-agriculture, agroforestry, biochar and enhanced-rock-weathering credits across the Global South.
backers: Founders Madhur Jain (CEO), Ankita Garg, Vishal Kuchanur. Series B led by WestBridge Capital (its first climate-tech bet); existing investors RTP Global and Omnivore participating.
funding: $20M first tranche of a targeted $45M Series B, led by WestBridge Capital (announced Feb 3, 2026), with RTP Global and Omnivore. Prior Series A ~$8.7M. Revenue Rs430M FY25, forecast Rs2B FY26.
traction: ~170,000-175,000 farmers across ~1.7M acres in India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Bhutan and Ivory Coast; >2M tonnes CO2 removed across 14 projects, ~150,000 credits issued. Offtake deals with Google, Microsoft, Lufthansa, Swiss Re, Capgemini.
reviews: Positive: credible Global South MRV leader with marquee buyers and a 90%-cost-cut remote-sensing pitch; WestBridge entry seen as strong validation. Negative: sector under heavy scrutiny — rice/methane and soil-carbon credits face additionality/quality concerns and questions about shallow (<30cm) sampling rigor; tied to a volatile voluntary carbon market.
pricing: Project-developer model: shares credit revenue with farmers, sells verified credits to corporates; MRV is the verification backbone. Per-credit pricing varies (n/a).
endo_take: Highest-momentum India-rooted soil-carbon player and a natural partner/channel — Endo's low-cost soil sensors and ETP/STP carbon hardware could feed Varaha's MRV pipeline rather than compete. Strong build-vs-partner case to supply ground-truth measurement.
justification: Best-funded India soil-carbon MRV leader with blue-chip buyers.

name: Boomitra
what_it_is: California-based (India-rooted founder) soil-carbon MRV and credit marketplace using satellite imagery + AI to estimate soil organic carbon, cutting field-sampling costs ~90%, and issuing verified credits for smallholders across the Global South. 2023 Earthshot Prize winner.
backers: Founder/CEO Aadith Moorthy. Investors incl. Yara Growth Ventures (lead), Chevron Technology Ventures, Global Innovation Fund, Jerry Yang, Tom Steyer and Kat Taylor.
funding: ~$11M equity raised (incl. a ~$4M 2021 round led by Yara Growth Ventures; Global Innovation Fund equity), plus a new ~$35M in project financing to scale operations across 5M+ acres in 9 countries. No large new priced equity round disclosed (latest equity round: n/a).
traction: 150,000-175,000 farmers across 5M+ acres in 9 countries on four continents; ~10M tonnes CO2 removed. Set a record with 3.03M Verra-issued soil-carbon removal credits from its Northern Mexico grassland project; issued first India soil-carbon credits (with Social Carbon); expanded to Costa Rica and to Argentine grasslands (with Rio Tinto / BirdLife) and launched its first biomass carbon-removal project.
reviews: Positive: Earthshot Prize and TIME100 recognition; lauded for satellite-only low-cost MRV, record-setting Verra issuances and returning ~70% of credit revenue to farmers. Negative: satellite-modeled carbon still draws methodological skepticism on accuracy/additionality, the soil-carbon-credit market remains soft and volatile, and equity funding is modest relative to its multi-continent ambitions.
pricing: Marketplace model — sells verified credits to corporate/government buyers; farmers receive ~70%. No per-credit list price (n/a).
endo_take: Strong India-active MRV partner whose satellite-only approach is precisely where cheap ground-truth soil sensors add credibility — and its record Verra issuance plus $35M project finance show real execution momentum. Clear partner/opportunity, not a competitor.
justification: Award-winning low-cost satellite soil-carbon MRV now setting record credit issuances and scaling via project finance.

name: TerraBlaster
what_it_is: Stealth-to-public agtech building rugged Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) sensors that drag behind a tractor/ATV ~6 inches deep to map pH and NPK (plus micronutrients) in real time, aiming to replace slow, sparse lab soil sampling.
backers: Founders Jorge Heraud (ex-Trimble precision-ag lead; Blue River Technology co-founder, sold to John Deere for $305M) and Matt Colgan (ex-Blue River/See & Spray). Investors: Khosla Ventures (lead), Trailhead Capital, Bidra/OCP Group VC arm, The Reservoir.
funding: ~$7M total disclosed: a $3M seed (as 'SoilCode' pre-rebrand) plus an oversubscribed $4M pre-seed led by Khosla Ventures (announced August 2025). Now raising a $10-15M seed to scale.
traction: Pre-commercial: moved from concept to field-validated prototype; commercial launch targeted late 2026. No paying customers yet. Strong industry signal via Heraud's pedigree.
reviews: No user reviews (not shipping). Industry reception strong — covered as a standout 2025 agtech launch; Heraud calls it 'the number one opportunity in agtech.' Skepticism centers on whether LIBS hardware can be miniaturized/cheapened enough and survive harsh field conditions at tractor speed.
pricing: n/a — hardware price still being finalized; stated goal is to not exceed what farmers currently pay for conventional soil sampling.
endo_take: Direct capability threat in real-time NPK sensing, but LIBS is high-cost/high-power and aimed at large mechanized US/EU farms — not Endo's low-cost smallholder niche, so more a tech north-star than a buy/partner. Watch their cost trajectory closely.
justification: Best-in-class real-time NPK tech, but closed hardware mismatched to Endo's market.

name: Yard Stick PBC
what_it_is: Handheld spectrometer probe that measures soil organic carbon stocks in situ (validated to ~45cm depth) in seconds, replacing slow, costly lab combustion testing for carbon MRV.
backers: Investors include Toyota Ventures Climate Fund, Microsoft Climate Innovation Fund, The Nature Conservancy, Lowercarbon Capital, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Pillar VC; plus ARPA-E grant support.
funding: $10.6M Series A (2023, led by Toyota Ventures Climate Fund) plus a new $18M round announced July 2025 (~$28M+ disclosed total).
traction: Field-deployed across carbon-program acreage; published a peer-reviewed accuracy study with the Soil Health Institute validating in-field carbon measurement to ~45cm. Positioned as the leading low-cost soil-carbon MRV hardware play.
reviews: Positive: reputation strong in the soil-carbon/MRV community, bolstered by independent SHI validation (a credibility differentiator most sensor startups lack). Negative: value tightly coupled to volatile voluntary carbon-credit markets; less proven for general agronomy/NPK use.
pricing: n/a publicly — sells measurement-as-a-service into carbon programs rather than commodity hardware.
endo_take: Most relevant to Endo's soil-carbon hardware ambition — a validated, well-funded benchmark for low-cost in-field SOC measurement and a potential partner/reference design. Their SHI-validated accuracy bar is the standard Endo must hit to be credible in carbon MRV.
justification: Validated, well-funded soil-carbon MRV leader — the bar Endo's carbon hardware must clear.

name: Blues (Notecard / Notehub)
what_it_is: Maker of the Notecard — a prepaid cellular/Wi-Fi/LoRa/satellite IoT module — paired with Notehub, a secure cloud data-routing and device-management service. Drop-in connectivity-plus-cloud for hardware builders.
backers: Founded by Ray Ozzie (ex-Microsoft CTO, Lotus Notes creator). Latest round led by Sequoia Capital (Roelof Botha joined the board).
funding: $25M round led by Sequoia Capital, announced May 20, 2025; substantial prior venture funding (total in the tens of millions).
traction: Broad developer/maker and industrial adoption; expanded global satellite coverage with Starnote for Iridium (Sept 2025) for fallback connectivity in remote areas. Sequoia lead and Botha board seat are strong scale signals.
reviews: Positive: developer sentiment notably good — transparent no-subscription 'freemium' consumption pricing, simple integration, global connectivity. Negative: usage-based event pricing can be hard to forecast at scale, and you pay on data egress from Notehub.
pricing: Notecard hardware ~$49 (lower-cost ~$10 Wi-Fi option); Notehub freemium — 5,000 free events/month, then ~$0.00075 per event (charged on egress).
endo_take: Strongest buy-vs-build candidate for Endo's connectivity layer — a Sequoia-backed, satellite-capable module that could connect rural Indian soil/ETP sensors off-the-shelf, though per-Notecard BOM (~$49) may be too high for ultra-low-cost smallholder units. Prototype with it, evaluate cost at scale.
justification: Drop-in, well-funded sensor connectivity with rural/satellite reach — easy partner, BOM-cost gate.

name: Memfault (acquired by Nordic Semiconductor)
what_it_is: End-to-end embedded observability, fleet health monitoring, and secure OTA firmware-update platform for connected devices — lets hardware teams catch, triage and fix field bugs and push updates remotely.
backers: YC-backed; raised from venture investors across Series A/B. Acquired June 24, 2025 by Nordic Semiconductor (low-power wireless chip leader), now embedded into Nordic's nRF Cloud.
funding: ~$35M raised over 3 rounds ($8.5M Series A, $24M Series B) before being acquired by Nordic Semiconductor (June 2025).
traction: Large-scale connected-product deployments across consumer/industrial IoT; post-acquisition, observability + OTA now offered out-of-the-box to all Nordic nRF customers via nRF Cloud (Sept 2025) — a major distribution expansion.
reviews: Positive: strong developer reviews (4+ stars on Capterra/marketplaces) for OTA, debugging and support. Negative: weak fine-grained access control — every user can access nearly all functions, a concern for production fleets needing restricted OTA permissions.
pricing: Free for 10 devices (non-production); pay-as-you-go from ~$0.10 per device per month, with enterprise tiers.
endo_take: Best-in-class drop-in for Endo's device-management/OTA needs and cheap to start — buy/integrate rather than build fleet observability in-house. The Nordic acquisition is a strategic signal: if Endo standardizes on Nordic nRF MCUs, this comes largely bundled.
justification: Best-in-class OTA/observability, cheap entry, now bundled with Nordic chips — clear buy.

name: DEEPX
what_it_is: South Korean fabless startup making low-power edge NPUs (DX-M1, 25 TOPS at 1-5W) for on-device AI in robotics, cameras and industrial/IoT devices. Available as cheap M.2/HAT modules for Raspberry Pi and x86/ARM hosts.
backers: Founder/CEO Lokwon Kim (ex-Apple, Cisco, IBM); investors SkyLake Equity Partners (lead), BNW Investments, AJU IB, TimeFolio Asset Management.
funding: $80.5M Series C at a $529M valuation (May 2024) led by SkyLake; cumulative private funding ~$531M. Hired Morgan Stanley in 2025 for a pre-IPO round; targeting an IPO around 2027.
traction: Mass production began mid-2025; ~350-company PoC pipeline and 27 confirmed purchase orders across 8 countries within 7 months. Distributed via Avnet, DigiKey, WPG; module partners Radxa, Sixfab, DFRobot; production partners AAEON, Advantech, Hyundai Robotics.
reviews: Positive: strong perf-per-watt (25 TOPS at ~3W), low module cost, supports TensorFlow/PyTorch/ONNX and modern models (YOLO, ViT, VLMs). Negative: young toolchain still maturing, heavy reliance on partner integration vs turnkey, and limited direct India presence so support/localization unproven.
pricing: Hardware sales: Sixfab AI HAT+ 13-TOPS ~$63, 25-TOPS ~$90; Radxa AICore module ~$187. No per-device licensing surfaced.
endo_take: Strong buy/partner candidate: cheap, low-power, Pi-compatible NPU modules let Endo add on-device vision/anomaly AI to sensors without designing silicon. Best fit of the edge-AI options for Endo's cost-sensitive, low-power form factor.
justification: Cheap low-power NPU, drop-in modules, fast commercial ramp.

name: SiMa.ai
what_it_is: San Jose firm building MLSoC chips (sub-10W) and Palette software for 'physical AI' across robotics, industrial automation, automotive and smart vision. The Modalix line adds generative/edge-LLM capability.
backers: Founder/CEO Krishna Rangasayee (ex-Xilinx); investors Maverick Capital (lead), StepStone Group, Fidelity, Dell Technologies Capital, Amplify Partners, plus strategic investor Micron.
funding: $85M round Aug 2025 led by Maverick Capital with new investor StepStone, bringing total to ~$355M; strategic investment from Micron disclosed April 2026 (amount undisclosed).
traction: ~232 employees (early 2026). Customers/partners include Kontron, Cerence AI, Enclustra and L&T Technology Services (Indian engineering giant). SoMs with Micron memory shipping for robotics/industrial/AV.
reviews: Positive: very low power (<10W) for the perf class, push-button Palette toolchain, production-ready DevKit 2.0. Negative: independent third-party reviews scarce (mostly first-party marketing); deployment friction from Docker/firmware/IT; aimed higher up the power/cost curve than Endo's tiniest sensor nodes.
pricing: Chip/module + DevKit hardware sales plus Palette software; DevKit 2.0 via online store, enterprise pricing on request.
endo_take: Partner/watch rather than core buy: excellent for heavier edge-vision or robotics gateways, and its L&T tie-up gives an India on-ramp, but sub-10W is still high for battery soil sensors. Better fit for Endo's ETP/STP industrial edge boxes than field nodes.
justification: Best-in-class physical-AI silicon, well-funded, but power/cost overshoots tiny sensors.

name: Sateliot
what_it_is: Barcelona-based LEO satellite operator delivering standards-based 5G NTN NarrowBand-IoT (3GPP Release 17) connectivity, letting standard NB-IoT devices roam to satellite where there is no cellular coverage. Targets agriculture, livestock, utilities and environmental sensing.
backers: Backed by the Government of Spain (~18.7% stake); investors include Global Portfolio Investments, Cellnex (early), and public co-financing partners. Co-founder/CEO Jaume Sanpera.
funding: Total ~$77.7M historically; closed EUR70M Series B (March 2025) and launched a EUR100-116M public/private Series C (April 2026) with up to ~50% public match-funding to deploy the constellation.
traction: Six satellites launched, five more planned in 2026; full constellation targeted 2027/2028. ~400 clients in 60 countries and ~EUR270M in precontracts; operator deals with Telefonica, Deutsche Telekom, Telenor IoT (May 2026), Turkcell demo. Won GSMA Foundry x ESA 6G Innovation Challenge (March 2026).
reviews: Positive: genuine standards-based (no proprietary modems) NB-IoT-over-satellite, strong telco partner roster, explicit agriculture/remote focus. Negative: pre-full-constellation, so coverage today is intermittent (store-and-forward, not real-time until 2027/2028); capital-intensive and partly government-dependent; no confirmed India deployment yet.
pricing: Wholesale connectivity sold via MNO/MVNO partners 'at a fraction of current satellite prices'; up to 50% subsidy on agriculture projects. No public per-device tariff.
endo_take: Strategic partner for Endo's rural reach: standards-based NB-IoT satellite could give Endo soil/ETP sensors connectivity in Indian fields with no cellular, but it's accessed via MNO partners and full coverage isn't until ~2027/2028. Watch and pilot, don't depend on yet.
justification: Standards-based satellite IoT for off-grid farms, but constellation immature.

name: Onomondo
what_it_is: Copenhagen-based cellular IoT connectivity provider with its own cloud-native core network and a global non-steered SIM/eSIM that auto-connects to the strongest of ~650-700 carrier networks across 180+ countries, with native cloud (AWS) integrations and traffic visibility.
backers: Founded 2012; investors include Verdane (lead), Maersk Growth, People Ventures, and the Danish Growth Fund.
funding: ~$31.5M total over 9 rounds; largest disclosed is a $21M Series A (June 2022) led by Verdane. No larger round confirmed since.
traction: 500+ customers across 62 countries; revenue grew 115% in 2024 (after 84% in 2023). Owns its core network connected to ~700 networks in 180+ countries; AWS Marketplace and Gartner/G2 listings.
reviews: Positive (G2/Gartner): non-steered SIMs avoid weak-network lock-in, strong traffic visibility, simplifies IIoT fleet management. Negative: per-SIM price above average, pricelist hard to find, occasional network blackouts, and slow initial network registration reported.
pricing: Pay-as-you-go per-MB data, no minimums or hidden fees; SIM/eSIM hardware plus usage. Reviewers find tariffs above average.
endo_take: Easy drop-in buy for Endo's cellular-connected sensors: a single global SIM with non-steered roaming and AWS integration simplifies multi-region deployments, though for India-only fleets a local LPWAN/cellular MVNO may undercut its above-average per-SIM cost.
justification: Turnkey global IoT SIM, easy adoption, but pricier than local options.

name: Fasal
what_it_is: Indian full-stack precision-ag startup combining patented on-farm IoT sensors, AI agronomy models and automation for horticulture crops (grapes, pomegranate, banana, chili). The closest direct domestic peer to Endo's soil/agri-IoT stack.
backers: Founders Shailendra Tiwari and Ananda Verma. Investors: TDK Ventures and British International Investment (BII) co-led latest round; existing backers 3one4 Capital, Omnivore, Wavemaker Partners, Genting Ventures, The Yield Lab Asia Pacific, ITI Growth Opportunities, Navam Capital, Aureolis Ventures.
funding: ~$19.4M total raised. Latest: ~INR 100 Cr (~$12M) Series A co-led by TDK Ventures and BII (reported late 2025/early 2026).
traction: IoT devices deployed across 150,000+ acres (~12% of India's grape land, ~8% of pomegranate); active in Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Himachal; expanding into Southeast Asia via FasalJet/FasalJet Pro. Claims 82.8B liters of irrigation water saved and 30-40% irrigation reduction in documented cases.
reviews: Positive: strong farmer outcomes (water/pesticide reduction, +30% yield/quality), patented hardware, real customer scale. Negative: heavy dependence on farmer trust-building and hand-holding; challenge translating complex data into simple advice; still horticulture-niche and modestly funded vs global peers.
pricing: Subscription/SaaS + hardware (device + agronomy advisory subscription per plot); specific pricing not public.
endo_take: Most direct India competitor and a useful benchmark; potential partner for crop-specific agronomy layered on Endo's lower-cost sensing, but also a head-to-head threat in horticulture belts.
justification: Proven India IoT peer, freshly funded by TDK/BII.

name: DigitalPaani
what_it_is: Gurugram IoT + software platform that digitizes and optimizes effluent (ETP) and sewage (STP) treatment-plant operations using sensors, panel data and AI-driven operating parameters. Direct adjacency to Endo's industrial ETP/STP water-monitoring line.
backers: Founders Mansi Jain and Rajesh Jain (father-daughter). Investors: Enzia Ventures (lead), Climate Angels Fund, Peer Cheque, Bharat Founders Fund, plus angels Ashish Goel (Urban Ladder), Alok Mittal (Indifi), Mohit Tandon (Delhivery), Mohit Sadani (Mom's Co).
funding: ~$1.2M seed (led by Enzia Ventures), reported recent/2025-2026.
traction: Deployed at 40+ enterprises including Tata Power, Delhi Jal Board, Britannia, Leela Hotels; targeting 150-175 plants and ~4,000 buildings across India and internationally by 2026. Team ~36.
reviews: Positive: blue-chip industrial/municipal logos, clear regulatory tailwind (CPCB real-time effluent mandates), water-neutrality angle resonates with ESG buyers. Negative: very small (seed-stage, lean team), single-vertical, unproven at its targeted plant-count scale; capital-light vs the buildout required.
pricing: SaaS subscription per plant plus IoT hardware/integration; pricing not publicly disclosed.
endo_take: The clearest India peer to Endo's ETP/STP IoT ambitions and a strong partner/acqui-target given its software/ops layer atop sensing; watch closely as both a collaborator and a competitor for industrial water accounts.
justification: Direct ETP/STP IoT peer, strong logos, seed-thin.

name: CropX acquires Acclym (formerly Agritask)
what_it_is: In Sept 2025 soil-sensor leader CropX acquired enterprise ag-intelligence platform Acclym (formerly Agritask), adding supply-chain sustainability/traceability software to its full-stack soil-sensing + farm-management platform. CropX's seventh acquisition.
backers: Acquirer CropX (backed by Aliaxis, OurCrowd, Innovation Endeavors; ~$90M+ raised). Acclym had raised ~$42M from Liechtenstein Group, Bridges Israel, Smart Agro Fund.
funding: Deal value undisclosed; announced 2 Sept 2025. Acclym brings ~$42M of prior venture funding and deployments across millions of hectares.
traction: Combined entity serves enterprise F&B brands for sustainability/regenerative-supply-chain monitoring; Acclym deployed across millions of hectares; CropX operates a multi-acquisition global soil-sensing + agronomy platform.
reviews: Positive: aggressive roll-up building an enterprise-grade soil-to-supply-chain stack; agronomist-grade support praised. Negative: serial-acquisition integration risk across seven companies; CropX's own last equity round was 2023, so consolidation may reflect a tougher funding climate rather than pure strength.
pricing: n/a
endo_take: Signals where full-stack ag-IoT is heading: sensing alone is commoditizing and value is migrating to enterprise sustainability/supply-chain software. A threat at the high end, but validates Endo owning a software/carbon layer rather than just hardware.
justification: Sensing-to-software roll-up; strategic signal, integration-heavy.

name: Miraterra acquires Trace Genomics + $16M raise
what_it_is: Vancouver soil-intelligence firm Miraterra acquired soil-DNA startup Trace Genomics' IP, products and Ames, Iowa lab (July 2025), then closed an oversubscribed ~$16M CAD round (early 2026) to scale its Raman-spectroscopy + AI 'Digitizer' for soil biological/chemical/physical measurement aimed at carbon markets.
backers: Acquirer/raiser Miraterra. Round led by At One Ventures, with Farm Credit Canada (follow-on), S2G Investments (S2G Ventures), the Sitka Foundation and iSelect.
funding: ~$16M CAD round (exceeded ~$13.9M target), led by At One Ventures, ~early 2026. Trace Genomics asset/IP acquisition (July 2025) value undisclosed.
traction: Acquired Trace Genomics' in-market soil-DNA products and Ames lab; positioning as a frontrunner for MRV in carbon markets, sustainability programs and supply-chain verification; expanding from soil into plant and food measurement.
reviews: Positive: differentiated Raman + AI hardware approach to low-cost soil MRV, strong climate-focused investor syndicate, consolidating soil-biology IP. Negative: early commercial stage and modest round size; Trace Genomics' prior 'independent growth wasn't sustainable' underscores how hard standalone soil-carbon measurement economics remain.
pricing: n/a
endo_take: Most strategically relevant deal to Endo's soil-carbon hardware ambitions; shows credible capital and consolidation in low-cost soil MRV. Worth tracking as a build-reference (or future tech-licensing partner) since their Raman+AI approach competes with cheap-sensor MRV Endo targets for India.
justification: Soil-carbon MRV consolidation, well-backed, early-stage.

name: Krishitantra (Krishi RASTAA)
what_it_is: Hyderabad-based agri-IoT startup whose portable 'Krishi RASTAA' device delivers a full soil-test panel — macronutrients, micronutrients, pH, EC, organic carbon and microbial counts — in ~30 minutes in the field, replacing slow government/lab soil testing for farmers, FPOs and agribusinesses.
backers: Co-founders Sandeep Kondaji, Vishnuprasada Bhat, Anand Bellan Raman. Investors: Omnivore (lead), NABVENTURES (NABARD's VC arm), SINE (IIT Bombay incubator).
funding: ~$1.18M total over ~4 rounds from ~12 investors, anchored by a $1M seed led by Omnivore and NABVENTURES. No large new priced round disclosed 2025-26 (latest round: n/a).
traction: 18,000+ farmers have used Krishi RASTAA; recommendations cut farmer input costs 12-28%. Hyderabad-based, expanding across India with plans to enter Southeast Asia. Sells via FPO / agribusiness / govt-scheme channels.
reviews: Positive: rare India-built rapid in-field soil-lab with credible NABARD/Omnivore backing and real cost-savings outcomes; strong fit for India's soil-health-card ecosystem. Negative: very thinly funded vs global peers, single-product, and rapid wet-chemistry-style testing faces accuracy/throughput scrutiny vs full lab assays.
pricing: Device + per-test / advisory service model sold to FPOs, agri-input firms and govt programs; list pricing not public (n/a).
endo_take: Closest direct India peer to Endo's low-cost soil-sensing thesis — both a competitive benchmark and a possible partner/channel via its FPO network. Validates demand for affordable in-field soil testing in India; watch their accuracy and unit economics closely.
justification: India-built rapid in-field soil lab with NABARD/Omnivore backing, but thinly funded.

name: Seqana
what_it_is: Berlin-based earth-observation + ML SaaS providing soil-organic-carbon (SOC) measurement, reporting and verification ('MRV-as-a-service') for regenerative-agriculture and carbon-farming projects, using satellite imagery plus a large proprietary ground-truth dataset to cut MRV cost.
backers: Founders incl. CEO; investors High-Tech Gruenderfonds (HTGF, lead), Counteract, ReGen Ventures, plus angels Stefan Gross-Selbeck and Axel Stepken. EU-funded research support.
funding: ~EUR2.1M seed (May 2024) led by HTGF and Counteract with ReGen Ventures. No larger round disclosed since (latest round: n/a).
traction: 5M+ hectares analyzed; leverages 1M+ proprietary and public ground-truth data points; positioning as a global MRV-as-a-service supplier across 6 continents for carbon-farming developers and corporates.
reviews: Positive: credible science-led satellite SOC MRV with strong climate-VC and EU backing, targeting the central cost barrier in carbon farming. Negative: very early/seed-stage and lightly funded; satellite-modeled SOC shares the accuracy/additionality skepticism dogging the whole soil-carbon-credit sector.
pricing: MRV-as-a-service / SaaS to project developers and corporates; per-hectare or project pricing not public (n/a).
endo_take: Natural software partner where Endo's cheap in-field soil sensors supply the ground-truth that satellite-only SOC models need for credibility. Lightly funded, so a partner/reference rather than a threat — Endo could be a data supplier into its MRV pipeline.
justification: Science-led satellite SOC MRV, well-syndicated but still seed-stage.

name: Golioth
what_it_is: Commercial IoT device-management and infrastructure platform ('IoT infrastructure as code') offering device fleet management, OTA firmware updates, data routing and cloud integration for embedded teams — a managed SaaS that connects and operates large device fleets.
backers: Founder/CEO Jonathan Beri (ex-Particle, Google Nest, WeWork). Investors Blackhorn Ventures, Zetta Venture Partners, Differential, MongoDB Ventures. Acquired by Canonical (the company behind Ubuntu) in 2025.
funding: Venture-backed (seed/Series rounds via Blackhorn, Zetta, MongoDB; amounts not fully disclosed). Strategic exit: acquired by Canonical in 2025 (deal value n/a).
traction: Listed on Google Cloud Marketplace; ST and Nordic ecosystem partner; now part of Canonical/Ubuntu, giving it open-source distribution and enterprise reach. Positive G2 developer reviews.
reviews: Positive: developers praise the clean API, infrastructure-as-code workflow, OTA and Zephyr/RTOS support; Canonical acquisition adds longevity and scale. Negative: still a relatively small platform vs hyperscaler IoT suites; post-acquisition roadmap/independence and pricing evolution are open questions.
pricing: Freemium SaaS with a free developer tier, then usage/device-based paid tiers; available via Google Cloud Marketplace billing. Exact enterprise pricing on request.
endo_take: Strong buy/integrate candidate for Endo's device-management and OTA layer — Zephyr-friendly, marketplace-billed, and now de-risked by Canonical's backing. Build-vs-buy leans buy; a credible alternative to Memfault/Blues for the fleet-ops stack.
justification: Easy-to-adopt fleet/OTA platform, now Canonical-backed for longevity.

name: BrainChip (Akida)
what_it_is: Australian (ASX-listed) neuromorphic computing firm whose Akida processors and IP run event-based, always-on AI at ultra-low power. The new AKD1500 co-processor delivers ~800 GOPS under 300mW, aimed squarely at battery-powered smart sensors, wearables and IoT nodes.
backers: Founder Peter van der Made; ASX-listed (public float) rather than classic VC. Strategic customers/partners include Neuromorphyx, HaiLa (RFIC), Quantum Ventura, and reference designs on Nordic Semiconductor MCUs.
funding: ~$25M (USD) capital raise announced Dec 2025 ahead of CES to commercialize Akida and fund Akida 2 / on-device GenAI. Publicly traded; market-funded beyond this raise.
traction: AKD1500 launched at Embedded World NA; AkidaTag reference platform (on Nordic) for always-on tags — evaluation May 2026, volume Q3 2026. Partnerships across defense, industrial sensing and cyber (Quantum Ventura); commercial revenue still early.
reviews: Positive: best-in-class performance-per-watt for always-on edge inference (sub-300mW), event-based sensing ideal for battery devices; growing partner roster. Negative: neuromorphic toolchain is niche and harder to adopt than standard NPUs; years of thin commercial revenue and a long road-to-volume have drawn investor skepticism.
pricing: IP licensing + chips/modules (AKD1500 co-processor, reference platforms); per-unit and license pricing not public (n/a).
endo_take: Most compelling tech for ultra-low-power always-on intelligence in battery soil/field nodes — but the neuromorphic toolchain and thin revenue make it a pilot/watch, not a core buy. For standard on-device AI, DEEPX is the easier path; keep Akida on the radar for the lowest-power sensing tier.
justification: Best-in-class always-on perf-per-watt, but niche toolchain and early commercials.

name: Lacuna Space (LoneWhisper)
what_it_is: UK satellite-IoT operator whose LoneWhisper Direct-to-Device (D2D) technology lets standard LoRa/LoRaWAN devices transmit small data packets directly to satellites from anywhere on Earth — no terrestrial coverage required — targeting smart agriculture, environmental monitoring, utilities and asset tracking.
backers: Founded ~2016; ESA / European space-program support; private investors (syndicate not fully disclosed). Co-founder Rob Spurrett.
funding: ~EUR20M invested over ~10 years of development. No single large 2025-26 round disclosed; pursuing a federated partner model rather than a big raise (latest round: n/a).
traction: Operational constellation expanded via June 2025 'Call of the Wild' launches; opening LoneWhisper D2D as a federated network for operator/national partners, with commercial launch around MWC 2026. Built on open LoRaWAN standards.
reviews: Positive: genuinely standards-based (works with off-the-shelf LoRa devices), long battery life, true global/off-grid reach, explicit agriculture focus. Negative: store-and-forward (not real-time), narrow uplink bandwidth, and access is via partners/operators rather than a turnkey self-serve service today.
pricing: Wholesale / partner model — connectivity sold through operator and national partners deploying LoneWhisper; no public per-device tariff (n/a).
endo_take: Direct-to-satellite LoRaWAN is a strong fit for Endo's off-grid Indian field sensors — standard LoRa hardware can reach orbit where there is no cellular. Pilot as a connectivity-fallback layer; complements Sateliot's NB-IoT-over-satellite approach, though it's partner-mediated and store-and-forward today.
justification: Standards-based LoRa direct-to-satellite for off-grid farms, but partner-mediated and not real-time.

name: AgroStar (Just Climate round)
what_it_is: AgroStar, a leading Indian omnichannel agtech platform (agronomy advisory + affordable agri-inputs + market linkages reaching 10M+ farmers), raised $30M led by Just Climate — the climate fund founded by Generation Investment Management — in Nov 2025, marking Just Climate's first India investment under its Natural Climate Solutions strategy.
backers: Founders Sitanshu Sheth and Shardul Sheth. New lead: Just Climate (Generation Investment Management). Existing backers Aavishkaar India, Bertelsmann, Evolvence India, Chiratae Ventures, Hero Enterprises.
funding: $30M equity round led by Just Climate (announced Nov 2025); part of a broader multi-round history. Use of funds: omnichannel expansion, input/output product innovation and AI.
traction: Reaches 10M+ farmers via 10,000+ retail stores and a direct-to-farmer digital platform. FY25 impact: ~276 billion litres of water saved and 120,000+ tCO2e emissions avoided through better soil health and reduced chemical-fertiliser use.
reviews: Positive: marquee global climate capital (Just Climate's first India bet) validates climate-smart Indian agtech at scale; deep farmer distribution. Negative: it's a distribution/advisory + inputs commerce model, not a sensing/hardware innovator — value is reach, not deep tech; thin-margin commerce business.
pricing: Commerce + advisory model: sells agri-inputs and advisory to farmers omnichannel; not a per-device/SaaS product.
endo_take: Not a sensing competitor but a massive India farmer-distribution channel and a strong signal that global climate capital (Just Climate) is now backing Indian climate-ag. Potential channel partner to deploy Endo's sensors/soil-health services to millions of farmers rather than a build-vs-buy decision.
justification: Just Climate's first India bet — major climate-capital signal for Indian agtech, but reach not deep tech.

name: Fyllo (AgriHawk Technologies)
what_it_is: Bengaluru agri-intelligence startup whose on-farm IoT devices (soil, climate and crop sensors) plus AI analytics and a farmer mobile app deliver real-time irrigation, nutrient and weather-risk guidance for horticulture and vineyards; has begun exporting its precision-farm processes to overseas vineyards.
backers: Founders Sachin Gautam, Sudhanshu Rai, Sumit Sheoran (founded 2019). Series A led by India Quotient and SIDBI Venture Capital; participants Ninjacart, IAN, Triveni Trusts, KIAORA, Titan Capital, 100X.VC, Venture Catalysts, Singularity Funds.
funding: ~$6.5M total over ~5 rounds; latest a ~$4M Series A (May 2024) led by India Quotient and SIDBI Ventures. No larger round disclosed since (latest round: n/a in 2025-26).
traction: On-farm devices deployed across Indian horticulture (grapes and other crops); expanding internationally, reportedly transferring its precision processes to foreign vineyards; hyperlocal weather models a differentiator. Hard revenue/acre figures n/a.
reviews: Positive: recognised as an early Indian precision-ag pioneer with real hardware + AI and overseas expansion; strong fit for high-value horticulture. Negative: modestly funded vs global peers, horticulture-niche, and like all advisory plays depends on farmer trust and hand-holding to convert data into action.
pricing: Device + advisory subscription (per-farm/per-plot); list pricing not public (n/a).
endo_take: Another direct India peer to Endo's soil/agri-IoT stack and a useful horticulture benchmark; possible partner for crop agronomy layered on Endo's lower-cost sensing, but also a head-to-head competitor in grape/vineyard belts.
justification: Established India precision-ag peer, Series A-funded but horticulture-niche and capital-light.

name: ChrysaLabs
what_it_is: Montreal-based maker of a handheld soil probe that uses optical spectroscopy plus AI to deliver instant in-field readings of macro- and micronutrients, pH, CEC, organic matter and moisture — and soil-carbon verification — replacing slow, sparse lab soil sampling.
backers: Founders incl. CEO Jean-Philippe Tremblay. Series A syndicate of ~11 investors (incl. agri/climate-focused funds and BDC-linked capital); full investor list not disclosed (n/a).
funding: ~CA$15M (~US$11M) total over 2 rounds; latest a CA$15M Series A (May 2023). No new round disclosed 2025-26 (latest round: n/a).
traction: Probe deployed with farmers and agronomists across North America; offered as a rental (~US$10,000/yr, unlimited probing sites) and positioned for both agronomy and low-cost soil-carbon verification. Revenue/scale figures n/a.
reviews: Positive: praised as instant, lab-comparable soil insight covering macro+micronutrients and carbon in one probe; flexible rental lowers adoption friction. Negative: spectroscopy-based nutrient accuracy faces the same calibration scrutiny as peers like Stenon; funding has been quiet since 2023, and ~US$10k/yr is steep for smallholders.
pricing: Rental ~US$10,000/yr (unlimited probing sites); no outright hardware list price (n/a).
endo_take: Direct capability/pricing benchmark for instant in-field nutrient + carbon sensing; its ~US$10k/yr rental shows the cost ceiling Endo must beat for Indian smallholders. A reference and possible tech partner, not a buy target.
justification: Instant spectroscopy soil probe covering nutrients + carbon, but pricey and quiet on funding.

name: Particle (acquired by Digi International)
what_it_is: Particle — a full-stack edge-to-cloud IoT platform-as-a-service (cellular/Wi-Fi modules + device cloud + fleet management) — was acquired by Digi International (announced Jan 27, 2026), folding a leading developer-friendly IoT platform into a public industrial-IoT hardware vendor.
backers: Particle founded by Zach Supalla; prior VC backers incl. Spark Capital, Root Ventures, Qualcomm Ventures. Acquirer: Digi International (NASDAQ: DGII).
funding: Acquisition announced Jan 27, 2026 (deal value n/a); Particle was at >$20M ARR at acquisition, with substantial prior venture funding (tens of millions; exact total n/a).
traction: >$20M ARR at acquisition; large developer and industrial customer base; now distributed through Digi's industrial-IoT hardware portfolio and channel for added scale and longevity.
reviews: Positive: developers value Particle's integrated modules + cloud + fleet tools and strong docs; the Digi deal is seen as validation and added enterprise reach. Negative: consolidation raises pricing/independence and roadmap questions, and Particle's per-device + data pricing has long been considered premium vs DIY stacks.
pricing: PaaS — free developer tier then per-device/month + data; cellular hardware modules sold separately. Enterprise on request.
endo_take: A buy-vs-build option for Endo's connectivity + fleet layer, now backed by Digi's industrial scale; the acquisition signals IoT-platform consolidation, so evaluate Particle/Blues/Golioth/Memfault as a set and watch for pricing lock-in.
justification: Leading IoT PaaS acquired by Digi — platform-consolidation signal and a solid drop-in option.

name: balena
what_it_is: Container-based (Docker-style) IoT fleet-management and OTA platform for deploying, updating and monitoring connected Linux devices and edge-AI workloads at scale, via balenaOS and balenaCloud.
backers: Founder/CEO Alexandros Marinos. New strategic growth investment from LoneTree Capital (NY growth fund, Jan 20, 2026); earlier backers incl. OpenView, Threshold/DFJ, Aspect Ventures, GE Ventures.
funding: Strategic growth investment from LoneTree Capital announced Jan 20, 2026 (amount n/a); ~$30M+ in prior venture funding.
traction: Supports 178 device types; powers fleets across 50+ countries, including customers with 100,000+ device fleets; the new capital is earmarked for edge-AI workloads and security/compliance features.
reviews: Positive: developers like the container/Docker model, balenaOS/balenaCloud workflow and broad board support; popular for edge-AI and Linux fleets. Negative: the Linux/container focus is heavier than MCU-class sensor nodes, and some find pricing and resource overhead high for very constrained devices.
pricing: balenaCloud freemium (free for small fleets), then per-device/month tiers; open-source balenaOS. Enterprise on request.
endo_take: Strong fit if Endo's ETP/STP edge gateways run Linux/containers and edge-AI — buy/integrate for those, though MCU-class field sensors are better served by Golioth/Memfault. Fresh growth capital and an edge-AI focus make it a credible fleet-ops option to evaluate.
justification: Container-based fleet/OTA platform, freshly recapitalized for edge AI, but Linux-heavy for tiny nodes.

name: Axelera AI
what_it_is: Eindhoven (Netherlands) edge-AI semiconductor startup whose Metis chip does ~214 TOPS at ~10W and whose next-gen Europa delivers ~629 TOPS (INT8), targeting computer vision and generative AI at the edge for industrial, robotics, retail, defence and vision systems.
backers: Founder/CEO Fabrizio Del Maffeo. Series C led by Innovation Industries with BlackRock and SiteGround Capital as new investors; existing backers Bitfury, CDP Venture Capital, EIC Fund, SFPIM (Belgium), Invest-NL, Samsung Catalyst Fund, Verve Investments.
funding: $250M Series C (Feb 24, 2026), led by Innovation Industries with new investor BlackRock — described as the largest investment ever in an EU AI-semiconductor company; ~$450M+ total raised in equity, grants and venture debt since 2021.
traction: Metis shipping via M.2/PCIe AI cards and systems to its ~500th global customer across physical/edge AI (industrial, retail, robotics, security, agritech); Europa next-gen in development. Strong scale signals post-raise; specific unit counts n/a.
reviews: Positive: standout perf-per-watt and a credible European alternative to Nvidia at the edge; BlackRock-backed mega-round is a major validation. Negative: aimed at ~10W vision/GenAI workloads — far above battery soil-sensor power budgets; software stack still young vs incumbents.
pricing: Hardware sales (M.2/PCIe AI cards, modules, systems) + SDK; enterprise pricing on request (n/a).
endo_take: Watch/partner for heavier edge-vision or ETP/STP industrial gateways, not battery field nodes — its ~10W class overshoots tiny sensors. The BlackRock-led mega-round shows edge-AI silicon is now seriously capitalized; for Endo's low-power tier DEEPX/BrainChip remain the better fit.
justification: Best-in-class edge-vision silicon and Europe's largest AI-chip raise, but power class overshoots sensor nodes.

name: Hailo
what_it_is: Israeli edge-AI processor maker whose Hailo-8 (26 TOPS at ~2.5W) and new Hailo-10 generative-AI accelerator bring high-efficiency on-device inference (edge LLMs and vision) to cameras, vehicles and industrial/IoT devices, with cheap Raspberry Pi-compatible modules.
backers: Founder/CEO Orr Danon. Extended Series C led by the Zisapel family with Automotive Equipment, Delek Motors and others; prior backers incl. Poalim Equity, Gil Agmon, ABB, Latitude Ventures.
funding: $120M extended Series C (announced with the Hailo-10 launch), bringing total raised to ~$340M at a ~$1.2B valuation; 300+ customers.
traction: 300+ customers; widely adopted Hailo-8/8L modules (M.2/Mini-PCIe and Raspberry Pi AI kits) across smart cameras, automotive and industrial vision; Hailo-10 generative-AI accelerator now launched.
reviews: Positive: among the most power-efficient production-grade edge-AI accelerators (26 TOPS at ~2.5W), with strong Raspberry Pi/maker availability and ecosystem; $1.2B valuation and 300+ customers signal real traction. Negative: vision-centric tooling and the ~2-5W class are still above ultra-low-power always-on sensor budgets, in a crowded edge-AI field.
pricing: Hardware sales — Hailo-8L M.2 modules ~$70-100; Raspberry Pi AI Kit (13 TOPS) ~$70; higher-TOPS modules more. SDK included.
endo_take: Strong buy/partner candidate alongside DEEPX for adding on-device vision/anomaly AI to Endo gateways — cheap, Pi-compatible, production-proven modules avoid silicon design. Best for camera/vision tasks; for the tiniest always-on nodes, BrainChip-class parts still win on power.
justification: Production-proven, cheap Pi-compatible edge-AI modules, well-funded at a $1.2B valuation — an easy buy.

name: Skylo
what_it_is: Mountain View NTN operator running the world's largest standards-based (3GPP Release 17) direct-to-device satellite network, delivering NB-IoT/D2D messaging to standard cellular chipsets where there is no terrestrial coverage — for agriculture, asset tracking, automotive and emergency messaging.
backers: Co-founders incl. Parthsarathi Trivedi. Series C led by NGP Capital; investors incl. Intel Capital, Innovation Endeavors, DCM, Boeing HorizonX, Samsung Catalyst, BMW i Ventures.
funding: $30M Series C (Feb 27, 2025, led by NGP Capital); ~$183M total over 4 rounds.
traction: Operates over EchoStar/Ligado/TerreStar L- and S-band; partnerships with Vodafone IoT, Soracom, Deutsche Telekom and chipset vendors; says it now reaches 1B+ devices and is the largest commercial standards-based D2D network.
reviews: Positive: standards-based (no proprietary modems), broad telco/MVNO and chipset partnerships, and real commercial scale today; explicit agriculture/IoT use. Negative: NB-NTN is narrowband, store-and-forward (not real-time, high-bandwidth); depends on partner spectrum/MNOs, and competes head-on with Sateliot and Lacuna.
pricing: Wholesale connectivity via MNO/MVNO and module partners (e.g., Soracom, Vodafone IoT); no public per-device tariff (n/a).
endo_take: Strong drop-in satellite-fallback option for Endo's off-grid field sensors — standards-based NB-NTN accessible via partners like Soracom/Vodafone, and more commercially live today than Sateliot or Lacuna. Pilot it as the connectivity backstop where cellular fails.
justification: Largest live standards-based D2D satellite-IoT network, partner-accessible, but narrowband.

name: CropIn
what_it_is: Bengaluru AI/SaaS agtech (founded 2010) whose platform digitizes farms via satellite imagery, weather, IoT and deep-learning models — crop monitoring, yield prediction and traceability — for agribusinesses, banks and governments globally, rather than selling sensing hardware directly.
backers: Founder/CEO Krishna Kumar. Investors incl. Google, JSR Corporation, ABC Impact, Chiratae Ventures, Alteria Capital and ~40 others.
funding: ~$54M total over ~17 rounds; a $14M round (2022) added Google and JSR; latest a small ~$0.81M tranche (Aug 2025). No large new priced round in 2025-26 (latest large round: n/a).
traction: Digitized 30M+ acres across 103 countries; 100+ B2B clients (SmartFarm used by 250+ agribusinesses in 52 countries). Aug 2025: won a EUR700K EIT Food contract to scale 'FIRST Potato' across Europe (pilots in Denmark, Germany, UK with Aarhus University).
reviews: Positive: deep, global, data/AI-led platform with marquee backers (Google) and a large enterprise footprint; strong on analytics and traceability. Negative: software/analytics-led (not a sensing-hardware innovator) — value is data not devices; fresh-funding momentum modest lately, and enterprise sales cycles are long.
pricing: Enterprise SaaS (per-acre/per-seat, project/contract-based); list pricing not public (n/a).
endo_take: A software/analytics layer that complements rather than competes with Endo's hardware — a potential partner to consume Endo's ground-truth sensor data into its AI models, and a benchmark for the India agtech-SaaS ceiling. More partner/opportunity than threat.
justification: Deep global India agtech-SaaS with Google backing, but software-led and quiet on fresh funding.

name: John Deere 2026 Startup Collaborators
what_it_is: John Deere named its 2026 Startup Collaborator cohort focused on soil sensing, edge AI and fleet monitoring — including resonAg (miniaturized MRI-based soil sensing), AIRS ML (on-device sensor-fusion edge AI) and IoTag (mixed-fleet telematics) — for year-long, project-based field pilots.
backers: Sponsor: John Deere (NYSE: DE). Cohort startups independently backed (syndicates n/a).
funding: Not an acquisition or investment vehicle — a structured year-long collaboration program (cohort announced 2026); deal values n/a.
traction: Deere's Startup Collaborator program has run for years as an on-ramp to its precision-ag ecosystem; the 2026 cohort gets field trials across Deere ag and construction use cases. resonAg adapts medical MRI-style sensing to soil; AIRS ML fuses sensing + ML on-device.
reviews: Positive: a strong signal that the world's largest ag-equipment maker is prioritizing soil sensing + edge AI, validating Endo's thesis, and selection is a credibility boost for the startups. Negative: collaboration, not capital — no guaranteed acquisition or revenue; Deere-centric (large-mechanized US/EU farms), distant from Indian smallholder economics.
pricing: n/a
endo_take: A market signal more than a buy/partner option: Deere betting on soil sensing + edge AI confirms where incumbents see value, and resonAg's MRI-style soil sensing is a tech to watch. Reinforces Endo owning the low-cost smallholder niche Deere won't serve.
justification: Big-incumbent validation of soil sensing + edge AI, but a pilot program, not capital.
